title: Achan (Joshua 7)
hook: one man's hidden theft brings trouble on everyone

segments.voice: Yesterday, teruah, the walls of Jericho, silence and then the shout. Your line was circle, then shout. Did you wait for the right moment to speak? Today, what someone carried out of Jericho. Day seven hundred three.

The book tells us the secret before anyone in the story knows it. Chapter seven opens: the children of Israel broke faith, because a man named Achan took things from Jericho that were forbidden, and hid them. Joshua has no idea. He sends a small force up to Ai, a little town, an easy win after Jericho. They run. Men die on the slope. And the hearts of the people melt like water, the same words Rahab used about Jericho's fear. Joshua tears his clothes and lies on his face before the ark until evening.
screen: `THE READER KNOWS FIRST.` → `DEFEAT AT AI.` → `JOSHUA ON HIS FACE.`

segments.voice: God's answer to Joshua is short: "Israel hath sinned." Not Achan. Israel. One man took, one man hid, and the text names the whole people. That's the first thing this chapter teaches, and it's uncomfortable on purpose. In this story nobody is purely private. What one person buries reaches everyone. Then comes the search, and it's slow. In the morning the tribes come forward, and one tribe is taken by lot. Then that tribe's families, and one family is taken. Then its households. Then its men, one by one. The circle narrows, step by step, and all through it, Achan says nothing. Only when the lot falls on him by name does Joshua speak to him, and he speaks gently: my son, give glory to God, tell me what you've done, hide it not from me. And Achan tells it, step by step. I saw. I coveted. I took. And they're hidden in the ground, inside my tent. Saw, wanted, took, hid: a whole hidden thing in one sentence. The ending is hard, and the text doesn't soften it: Achan and his household are stoned in a valley that gets the name Achor, trouble. The rabbis read the chapter's first verdict closely. The Talmud takes Israel hath sinned and notices the word Israel: even when Israel sins, the Talmud says, it is still Israel. Achan's wrong is called the people's, and the people keep their name.
screen: `ISRAEL HATH SINNED.` · `THE CIRCLE NARROWS.` · `SAW, COVETED, TOOK, HID.` · then, large: `STILL ISRAEL.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: admit one hidden thing to yourself. Not to anyone else. Just to you. Settle, and breathe. Let something come up that you've kept buried: a thing you took, a word you didn't say, a habit you'd rather no one saw. Don't argue with it, and don't fix it right now. Just name it, silently, in plain words, the way Achan finally did: I saw, I wanted, I took, I hid. Then breathe out, and let it be known, at least by you. The bell holds the time.
Achan. The man who hid what he took from Jericho, whose silence brought trouble on everyone, whose people are still called Israel. Today's word.
Your line: one hidden thing affects all. Today, notice one way a private choice of yours reaches someone else. Day seven hundred three.

howItsDone: Jewish confession on Yom Kippur is said in the plural, "we have sinned", by the whole congregation together, and the Talmud's reading of Achan's story is cited for the idea that a Jew who sins remains a Jew.

what it means: one man's hidden theft is named the whole people's sin, and the circle narrows until he speaks.
what a scholar hears: the Talmud reads Israel hath sinned and notices the name: even when he sins, he is still Israel (Sanhedrin 44a).

notes: The confession sequence saw, coveted, took, hid follows 7:21; confirm against the JPS text.
The echo of 'hearts melted' (7:5 and Rahab's 2:11) is noted; confirm wording of both verses supports it.
Sanhedrin 44a ('even though he sinned, he is Israel') is paraphrased; confirm.
Valley of Achor glossed as 'trouble', following the text's own wordplay in 7:25–26; flag under the strict etymology rule.
The stoning of Achan and his household (7:24–25) is named briefly; a Keeper may want different wording.
howItsDone: plural Yom Kippur confession (Ashamnu, Al Chet); confirm phrasing.
Editor: Sanhedrin 44a applies 'he is still Israel' to the people, not to Achan by name; teach and word reworded to match; 'often cited' in howItsDone softened.
